trust_decision.summary: A document may contain at most one DOCTYPE: a per-parse boolean is set at the single '<!D' branch of the main scan loop and a second '<!D' throws 'Multiple DOCTYPE declarations found.' before DocTypeReader.readDocType/EntityDecoder.addInputEntities run. The reason this matters is that every addInputEntities call zeroes the decoder's expansion budget (_totalExpansions, _expandedLength), so each extra DOCTYPE hands the attacker a fresh maxTotalExpansions/maxExpandedLength allowance. The decision is made in the parser, before the entities of the second declaration are registered.

landing_point.why: It is the only place a DOCTYPE is read and its entities are handed to the entity decoder, so an engineer who reads 'repeated DOCTYPE declarations reset entity expansion limits' starts exactly at this branch.

fix_sites.entry_point: XMLParser.parse (src/xmlparser/XMLParser.js:19) exported from src/fxp.js:10-14; deprecated CLI wrapper at src/cli/cli.js:57-58 uses the same call
fix_sites.module_kind: parser core (main scan loop); supporting state at src/xmlparser/OrderedObjParser.js:88-89 and :294-296

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only untouched carrier of the same check is lib/fxp.cjs, the generated CommonJS bundle: a solver can say it is build output covered by a rebuild, not a security site, and that the spec suite he just made pass imports src/.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A single DOCTYPE that declares several entities and is referenced many times must still parse and expand, and processEntities:{enabled:false} must still return the reference literally ('&test;'); a fix that refuses any DOCTYPE, drops input entities, or makes the entity count a hard document-wide deny breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: two or more '<!DOCTYPE ...>' declarations in one document, with or without an internal subset ('[...]')
repetition anywhere in the document (before, between or after the root element), not only in the prolog
repetition under processEntities enabled and under enabled:false (the guard is unconditional)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Package 'main' load path: require('fast-xml-parser') resolves to lib/fxp.cjs, whose bundled parseXml still calls entityDecoder.addInputEntities on every '<!DOCTYPE' with no repetition guard when the source fix is applied, so the packaged CommonJS API keeps the reset. lib/fxp.min.js, lib/fxparser.min.js and lib/fxvalidator.min.js are the same stale build.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: lib/ is generated output; the fix belongs in src/ and the package can be rebuilt, so the solver treats it as out of scope after making the src specs pass.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one generated file in a sibling directory of src/, reached through package.json:5

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second entity-input route in the same parser, e.g. a DOCTYPE handled on a streamed/buffered parse loop or an external-subset path that re-registers input entities
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already duplicated this scan loop once (src/v6/Xml2JsParser.js:44-80) and ships five separate webpack entry bundles (webpack.cjs.config.js:11-107), so a second parse entry is an ordinary way this codebase grows.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a document-wide entity budget next to the per-call entityCount so a later DOCTYPE cannot reopen the budget
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: entityCount is a local reset on every readDocType call (src/xmlparser/DocTypeReader.js:15), so a maintainer adding a global counter or a 'seen DTD' check there is a natural single-file change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the same repeated-DOCTYPE guard in the legacy v6 special-tag reader
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is an existing copy of the same DOCTYPE reader in the tree, and maintainers usually keep such copies in step when patching a parser.

O9_family: CWE-776 improper restriction of recursive entity references in DTDs (XML entity expansion / billion laughs)

O10_build.toolchain: npm with package-lock.json, jasmine 5.6 + c8 for tests, webpack 5 for the lib/ CJS/UMD bundles; no native or C++ dependencies
O10_build.project_tests: jasmine over spec/*spec.js via `npm test` (package.json:23); entity expansion limits and defaults are covered in spec/entities_security_spec.js:60-538 and entity replacement in spec/entities_spec.js; the CJS/UMD import tests in spec/importTests/ are not in the npm-test glob.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a boolean guard to the DOCTYPE branch of OrderedObjParser and validate with the src spec suite, leaving the shipped lib/ CJS and UMD bundles, which are the package main, unguarded.

out_of_scope_notes: src/v6 is an in-repo legacy parser with its own readDocType (src/v6/XmlSpecialTagsReader.js:39-83), no entity-expansion limits at all and no repeated-DOCTYPE state; it is not exported by package.json:10-21, docs/v4, v5/Security.md:31 calls it experimental and keeps reports there out of scope, and its entity registration is already broken (src/v6/XmlSpecialTagsReader.js:89 uses an undefined 'source'), so the advisory's limit-reset property does not apply to it; not pursued.
unverified: @nodable/entities is not vendored in this tree (no node_modules), so the counter reset is evidenced from the bundled copy at lib/fxp.cjs:1 (addInputEntities sets _totalExpansions=0 and _expandedLength=0) rather than from the dependency source.
